messages:
Courtney: Quick design question — for the new "Create Pipeline" form (long, 20+ fields): do we show inline errors as red badges next to labels, or use a single error summary at the top with anchor links? Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/create-pipeline Sam: Inline first, summary on submit fail. Users expect immediate feedback. Badges are good for scanning. Maria: Agree with Sam. Also accessibility: badges alone aren't announced by screen readers. Need aria-live or an alert region. Jon: Quick accessibility snippet: ```
Form has errors. 3 fields need attention.
Name required ``` Alex: +1 for assertive aria-live. Also consider focus management: move focus to first invalid field on submit. Courtney: Good call. What about required marker — a red asterisk vs the word "Required"? Contrast concerns. Maria: Asterisk only is terse but not clear for some users. Prefer `* Required` label text for key flows. Keep color separate from meaning. Sam: For destructive actions (bulk delete) — should we use typed-confirm e.g., type resource name, or modal + undo toast? Thoughts? Jon: If irreversible (no backup), typed-confirm. For quick ops where undo is possible, modal + undo toast is friendlier. accessibility-bot: Accessibility check: contrast for our "error red" (#d9534f) against white is borderline for 12px. Suggest #b00020 for AA. Courtney: Consensus so far: inline errors for typing, top summary on submit fail, aria-live assertive for announcement, focus jump to first error, use "* Required" in label and avoid color-only indicators. Typed confirm for irreversible deletes, modal+undo for recoverable actions. I'll update the Figma and RFC. Sam: thx! I'll add the code examples to the docs and ping when done :thumbsup: Maria: I'll run a quick keyboard/a11y pass once updates are in. Courtney: Filing follow-ups: design PR, dev PR, a11y audit. Assigned: @sam (dev), @maria (a11y).
